RecordingEnabled and GitignoreEntryAbsent, the four-shape GitignoreVariantsRefuseByteIdentical) PASS in 857s, exit 0. Worktree left byte-identical. G1-G4 verified delivered as the BRIEF describes from my lens: the enumeration is now honest (ComputeEntangleablePaths with the .gitignore entry-absence class and the per-spec recording class), -z parsing is confined to CheckDirtyTreeProportional (I diffed 953e9abb against the PRE-BEAD base: among pre-existing guard.go lines only the package var block changed to add statusPorcelainZFn — parsePorcelain, CheckDirtyTree/Detail, and DirtyTreeFailure are byte-identical to base, so release/complete semantics are untouched by construction), renames block on either side with the collapsed-untracked-dir ancestor rule, the presence bit is consumed with a fourth distinct output (per phaselock.go's phaseReadOutcome contract; regression test TestBackfillExistingEpicPhase_PresentButInvalidLeftUntouched), and my G5 wording pin landed at both levels. Bonus fixes judged under author-of-record: (1) the samePath anchor gate — claimAnchorRoot is a line-for-line faithful replication of MindspecExecutor.resolveAnchorRoot (mindspec_executor.go:1783-1801: same specID=="" early return, same config.Load-with-DefaultConfig fallback from the same root, same SpecWorktreePath call, same Stat+IsDir preference, same degrade-to-repoRoot), and I traced the claim path's only .gitignore write to DispatchBead's EnsureGitignoreEntry(anchorRoot,...) at mindspec_executor.go:305 (the :170 g.Root write is InitSpecWorkspace — plan-approve, not the claim path); the two e2e legs prove the anchor behavior empirically by having to seed and observe from the spec worktree. (2) StatusZWithStderr's separate stdout/stderr capture is correct and necessary (an advisory stderr warning must not splice into the NUL-delimited stream; stderr still folds into the error on genuine failure). (3) The two lint-ratchet entries mirror sibling justifications and carry real rationale. (4) mindspecCmdName satisfies the specgate literal constraint. HasGitignoreEntry is genuinely extracted FROM EnsureGitignoreEntry's own check (the ensure now calls it, so divergence is structurally impossible). The next.go Step 1.5 relocation is a byte-identical lift-and-shift of the resolve block. HOWEVER, two documentation-honesty defects remain at 953e9abb, and one of them sits in this bead's own MANDATORY deliverable: the ADR-0025 amendment (untouched by 953e9abb — no ADR file in the commit) still records the refuted round-1 derivation verbatim: 'the repo-relative paths a worktree-creating claim writes in the invoking checkout are, at this base, exactly (a)...(b)...(c)... The claim-entangleable user-dirt set is therefore EMPTY today', and its anti-drift paragraph still describes 'an explicit list (empty beyond the exempt artifact today)'. The round-1 panel proved exactly that derivation FALSE (the .gitignore and recording write classes), the fix shipped a conditional computed enumeration — and the governing ADR text this spec mandated now misdescribes the rule it exists to authorize, in a spec whose whole subject is state honesty. Second, ComputeEntangleablePaths' own header comment contradicts both its code and itself: bullet 2 claims the recording writes 'ALWAYS write under repoRoot (unconditionally — unlike the .gitignore write, this one does NOT route through resolveAnchorRoot)' and the observability paragraph says 'the recording class when repoRoot == cwd (its target is always repoRoot, unconditionally)' — but EmitMarker resolves via EventsPath → RecordingDir → workspace.SpecDir, which PREFERS the spec worktree's copy (workspace.go:478-491), the code correctly gates on samePath(anchor, cwd) (guard.go:144), the function's own inner comments (guard.go:132-137, 146-150) say so, and the RecordingEnabled e2e leg only passes BECAUSE the writes land in the spec worktree. A maintainer following the header would 'correct' the gate to repoRoot==cwd and break the exact case the e2e pins. guard.go:69's 'the real enumeration is empty today' is likewise stale. These are the remaining changes; the code itself is right and comprehensively proven.

findings.detail: 953e9abb touches no ADR file. At the reviewed commit, .mindspec/adr/ADR-0025-jsonl-as-build-artifact.md's amendment asserts the claim writes 'exactly (a) session.json (b) issues.jsonl (c) the worktree dir', concludes 'The claim-entangleable user-dirt set is therefore EMPTY today', and pins anti-drift to 'an explicit list (empty beyond the exempt artifact today)'. Round 1 proved that enumeration factually wrong (G1/F1/F1-R6: EnsureGitignoreEntry and the recording writes) and the fix shipped ComputeEntangleablePaths' two conditional classes with anchor gating. The governing ADR text — the artifact this spec made a mandatory bead deliverable precisely so the narrowed rule would be recorded honestly — now documents the refuted claim as if still true. The scope fence and notice paragraphs remain correct and should be kept.

findings.title: ComputeEntangleablePaths' header comment contradicts its own code (and its own inner comments) on where recording writes land
findings.detail: guard.go ~94-116 claims recording writes 'ALWAYS write under repoRoot (unconditionally — ... does NOT route through resolveAnchorRoot)' and that the class gates on 'repoRoot == cwd'. Verified false: EmitMarker → EventsPath → RecordingDir → workspace.SpecDir (workspace.go:478+) prefers the spec worktree copy whenever it exists; the code gates on samePath(anchor, cwd) at guard.go:144; the inner comments at :132-137/:146-150 state the SpecDir preference correctly; and TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_EnumerationPin_RecordingEnabled had to seed the manifest in the spec worktree and observe from there to pass. A maintainer trusting the header could rewrite the gate to repoRoot==cwd and break that pinned case. guard.go:69 ('the real enumeration is empty today') is similarly stale.
